findings.description: The query's `sort` convention is that a `-` prefix means descending, so an unprefixed value should mean ascending. The code computes `descending = sort.startswith('-')`, which is correct for that convention. The real problem is the default: `query.get('sort', '-placed')` keeps newest-first only when `sort` is absent. An explicit `sort=placed` therefore flips to ascending, which silently differs from the old default and from `orders_panel`'s own default of `descending=True`. Callers that pass `sort=total` or `sort=customer` get ascending results, while `orders_panel(sort='total')` gets descending. The two entry points disagree on the direction for the same column name.
findings.suggestion: Document and keep a single convention, or make the direction default consistent between `orders_panel` and `panel_from_query`.
findings.title: Sort direction defaults to descending for every column when no prefix is given

findings.description: If `status` is empty, or contains only commas or whitespace (e.g. `status=,`), the parsed list is empty and `or None` turns it into None, so no status filter is applied. A user who explicitly sent an empty filter gets every order instead of a rejection or an empty result. `orders_between` has a deliberate branch for an empty `statuses` list, and it is unreachable from this entry point.
findings.suggestion: Pass None only when the `status` key is absent; otherwise pass the parsed list, or raise ValueError for a blank value.
findings.title: Blank status parameter is treated as no filter
